Theme

Latin word

commodum

commodum, commodī n.

noun, second declension

advantage, a good point; the good one gets from a thing; just, just then; had just … (when)

In this lexicon

  • advantage

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. de Or. 2.335: commoda pācis … itemque incommoda contrāriōrum; Cic. Tusc. 1.30: orbātōs vītae commodīs

  • just now

    also used · classical · Plaut. Cas. 3.4.3: ad tē hercle ībam commodum, I was just coming to you (Lewis & Short); Cic. Att. 13.9.1 (Lewis & Short)

  • cum erit tuum commodum: at your convenience

    classical

  • commodum est: suit

    classical

Examples

  • quī ūtilitātem dēfendet, ēnumerābit commoda pācis, opum, potentiae, vectīgālium … itemque incommoda contrāriōrum

    whoever argues for advantage will list the advantages of peace, wealth, power and revenue … and likewise the disadvantages of their oppositesCic. de Or. 2.335

    In the entry for advantage

    there is great advantage in despising the very things that are fearedCic. Tusc. 4.64
